stage: Gate G1 is open (docs/chronicles/WORK_STATUS.md §5.2): these are kernel and material captures only, which the plan allows during the review. No scene is composed and no blueprint viewpoint is rendered yet; B4 and B5 composition starts once G1 is recorded.
renderer: Development harness main game/src/chronicles/scene/harness.html on Chromium headless with SwiftShader (software WebGL), 1920 x 1080. The clay sheets use a camera-relative key light. The Quest rows are an unlit preview with a stand-in vertex light, not the IWSDK runtime and not a headset.
captureScript: node scripts/chronicles/capture-archive-harness.mjs (it starts and stops its own dev server on port 5193)

reviews.assessment: All 24 kernel forms build alone and read as authored architecture: kite piers with an engaged shaft, base and impost mouldings and a capital; a stilted pointed arcade arch with voussoir joints, a basalt keystone, an arris roll and a hood; a gallery with balusters; mitred string course and cornice; the coffered octagon-to-round vault; eight ribs; the oculus ring with its bronze band; the star-pierced screen; bays, vestibule, recesses, lamps, dial, ring band, dais, stele and the parametric plinth. The pier body and the bay back walls are still fairly plain, and the ring band has a rectangular section.
fixedDuringReview: Arcade arch: voussoirs beyond the jambs had no extrados face, so joint faces showed as fins; the extrados is now closed where no spandrel covers it.
Vault shell: it was a plain dome. It now carries a stepped coffer grid, three coffers across each web, diminishing over four rows (three on Quest), each with a small bronze star boss.
Oculus screen: its bars now use dressed stone in their own slot, so the screen's alpha mask can no longer punch holes in them.

reviews.assessment: The same forms at Quest tessellation keep their silhouettes. Joints are not cut, the balustrade is a solid panel and the vault has three coffer rows. The kernel build totals 59,442 triangles against a 150,000 kernel budget.

Desktop PBR at 1024: coursed limestone ashlar with per-block tone, bedding and tooling; dressed limestone; carved rosette panels; dark veined floor stone; basalt with chisel strokes and pale crystals; bronze reading as metal with worn bright edges and a few verdigris spots; the star-pierced screen against the light; lamp, ring band and plinth combinations. The Quest rows show the baked-lit albedo at 512 under a stand-in vertex light.
fixedDuringReview: Bronze: dense engraved lines in the texture read as wooden planks. Engraving is left to the geometry, and the texture is now a cast skin with wear and patina spots.
Floor veins: the contrast was too strong at 3.2 m slabs and has been reduced by about 30%.
Reflections: the procedural environment's stone level was raised, so the metals reflect warm stone instead of black.
Periodic noise: anisotropic fields scaled coordinates and broke tiling at the texture seams. Every field now uses integer cell counts per axis.

reviews.assessment: Desktop at 512 and Quest at 256, with low tessellation. The materials hold their character at the smaller sizes, and the carved panels and the ashlar coursing stay legible.
Front view with edges: the arch tessellation is even, and the hood, roll and voussoirs are clean after the fix.
The closed extrados shows below the springing. Above it, the spandrel's open side at the jamb exposes the voussoir joints, but in the room that side sits inside the pier.
The pier's chamber face: kite plan, stepped base mouldings, an engaged shaft with its own base, and the impost band at the arch springing.
From below, the coffers diminish toward the oculus, and the bosses read as points of bronze. The carved frieze runs around the springing.
The coffer bands step twice, so each coffer reads as recessed. Bosses sit on the shell with no gap.
The string course wraps the first pier with mitred corners, and its cavetto and ovolo profile is visible.
The cornice wraps the pier: bed mouldings, a corona with a drip and a cyma crown, with clean mitres.

againstReferenceFrames: The reference frames set the bar for sunlit dappled light, warm saturated colour and rich material breakup. The materials now carry that breakup: ashlar coursing, veining, chisel work and patina. The dappled light depends on the key light's oculus cookie, which is generated (oculus-cookie-512.webp), and on the baked bounce. Neither can be judged until the scene is composed after G1, so lighting and atmosphere are not yet evidenced here.
